text:
Los Angeles scored first on a goal that barely deserved to count, and Florida spent the next two periods taking the game back. Alex Laferriere put LAK ahead at 19:00 of the first on an 8 percent wrist shot, but FLA out-chanced them 1.48 to 0.95 in expected goals in the second and tied it on Seth Jones's wrist shot at 3:49. Over the full game FLA's expected goals were 2.69 to LAK's 2.02, and they attempted 65 shots to 47.

Matthew Tkachuk settled it at 11:20 of the third, finishing a Sam Bennett feed with a wrist shot that was only a 6 percent chance. Tkachuk's line was on the ice for 1.52 expected goals for and 1.10 against, and he played 21:24 in a 2-1 FLA win. Neither team scored on the power play. FLA went 0 for 6 on chances worth 1.38 expected goals, and LAK went 0 for 5 on 0.53, so the man advantage never decided anything.

The goaltending shaped the margin. Jacob Markstrom stopped 19 of 20 and saved 1.0 goals more than his shots deserved, while Darcy Kuemper made 28 saves on 30 shots, 0.69 better than expected. Florida's simulated-replay win share was 62 percent to LAK's 38. LAK's best look came from Joel Armia, a 24 percent chance in the third that missed the net. The home team also gave the puck away 27 times to FLA's 15, which helps explain why the shot count tilted so far.
